  "text": "My father brought the broken toaster to my flat in a carrier bag.

“You’ve got tools,” he said.

“So have you.”

“Yours are easier to find.”

He put it on the kitchen table and spread newspaper beneath it. Crumbs fell from the slots as he turned it over.

I fetched the screwdriver set he had given me when I moved in. Each handle still had a small sticker on it.

He watched me choose one.

“Unplugged?” he asked.

I held up the loose cord.

“Good habit to check.”

The screws were tight. He kept his hands flat on the newspaper while I worked.

Inside, a spring had come loose. There was also a blackened piece of bread, thin and hard as a roof tile.

“Your mother liked it well done,” he said.

“She liked it brown.”

“She used to put it through twice.”

I tipped the burnt bread into my palm. He reached for it, then pointed at the bin.

We found where the spring belonged. It took both of us to stretch it into place, his finger holding one end while I hooked the other with pliers.

Afterward, I made toast.

He stood beside the machine until it popped, then carried the plate to the table.

“Works,” I said.

He scraped a dark corner with his knife.

When he left, the toaster was still on the counter.

“You forgot this.”

“Keep it. Yours only does two slices.”

“So does this one.”

He looked at it for a moment.

“Well,” he said. “Now you can have someone round.”"
